grids.aria: About 9 of 100 dots filled: 9.1% of first-year applicants were admitted

chances.src: Fall 2025 first-years (C1): 10,340 of 114,125 admitted (9.1%). NYU doesn't report an in-state split or its Early Decision numbers in the CDS.

ladder.title: 5 things are top-tier. Two of them are about who you are, not what you did.
ladder.lede: Your recommendation letters and your character sit right next to your grades. Activities are only "considered." So the people who write about you, and how your essay sounds, matter a lot here.
considered: First in your family to go to college
How interested you are in NYU
ladder.note: Top tier = where your hours go before Jan 1 or Jan 5 ↓
ladder.src: Section C7, first-year admission factors, 2025–26 Common Data Set. Programs that need an audition or portfolio rate it very important too.

numbers.lede: Type your GPA on a 4.0 scale to see where it sits next to NYU's first-years. This is a range, not a cutoff.

gpa.default: Average GPA of enrolled first-years: 3.81 on a 4.0 scale.
gpa.near: Right around NYU's average. Now your other top-tier rows decide it: your essay, your letters and your character.
gpa.above: Above NYU's average. Good start. Your essay and letters are top-tier too, so they still do heavy lifting.
gpa.below: Below NYU's average. That's not a no. Your essay, letters and character are all top-tier at NYU. Put your hours there.

facts.text: of enrolled first-years had a GPA of 3.75 or higher (17% had a 4.0).

money.title: If you qualify for aid, NYU meets about 100% of need for first-years.
money.lede: The sticker price isn't your price. NYU says families earning under $100,000 with typical assets won't pay tuition. The net price calculator gives a real estimate in about 15 minutes.
money.aid_line: About 1 in 4 first-years get need-based grants. First-years who got aid averaged $72,963 a year.
money.src: Costs: NYU 2026–27 estimated cost of attendance (NYU Bulletin); NYU's 2025–26 CDS leaves out section G. Aid: Section H2 (99.8% of need met for first-years; line J average package of first-years awarded aid). Under-$100K promise: NYU cost of attendance page. Food and housing (about $26,438) cost extra.

todo.title: 4 moves, all aimed at NYU's top tier.

items.title: Decide: Early Decision II or Regular Decision.
items.body: ED II (Jan 1) is binding. Only pick it if NYU is your first choice and your family has run the net price calculator.

items.title: Give your recommender a one-page cheat sheet.
items.body: Letters are top-tier at NYU. Send 3 things you want them to know, with one example each. Check your NYU portal for exactly what it asks for.

items.title: Read your Common App essay out loud.
items.body: Essays and character are both top-tier. If a sentence could be about anyone, cut it.

items.title: Answer the optional NYU essay.
items.body: It's 250 words about being a "bridge builder," and it's the only NYU-specific writing on the application. Character is top-tier here, so it's worth writing.

todo.done: All 4 done. That's a real application. ✓

title.s: Is your essay doing its job?
title.p: Is your student's essay doing its job?

lede.s: Essays and character are both top-tier at NYU. Here's what I looked for as an admissions reader. Read your Common App essay, then tap what's true.
lede.p: Essays and character are both top-tier at NYU. Here's what I looked for as an admissions reader. Read your student's Common App essay together, then tap what's true.

items.title: It answers the exact question asked.
items.body: Circle the key words in the prompt. Every paragraph should answer them, not a question close to them.

items.title: Only one person could have written it.
items.body: Swap in a friend's name. If it still works, it isn't specific enough yet.

items.title: It shows one real moment.
items.body: A scene beats a list of awards. The list already lives in the activities section.

items.title: A reader could sum it up in one line.
items.body: Readers spend a few minutes per file. Hand them the sentence they'll repeat when they argue for you.

after.s: Not sure you can check all four? That's normal. It's hard to judge your own essay.
after.p: Not sure? That's normal. It's hard to judge an essay you're close to.

self_check.all_done: All 4. Nice work. A fresh reader can still catch what you can't see.

take.heading: What I saw as an admissions reader
take.quote: At NYU, your letters and your character are rated as high as your grades. So your essay and your recommender should describe the same person. Pick one quality you want a reader to remember, and make sure both show it.
